samples.summary: `detachAnchor`'s `toJSON` branch can return the still-attached input object instead of falling through to the hand walk
samples.evidence: `unwrapJson` (yorkie-json.ts:22-33) only parses when `toJSON()` returns a *string*; for any other return it falls to `return value as T`, i.e. the original object. `detachAnchor` then sees `parsed && typeof parsed === 'object'` and returns that same undetached object as the anchor (line 109), never reaching the `detachYorkieValue` fallback the docblock promises. The result is an anchor that is still the live value in the response payload. Narrow (needs a `toJSON` that does not return a string) but the branch is written as if it always detaches.

samples.summary: The new `catch` in `detachAnchor` swallows a parse failure and falls back to `detachYorkieValue`, which the same file documents as producing garbage for array-carrying anchors
samples.evidence: `detachAnchor` catches the `parseJsonSnapshot` failure and falls through to `detachYorkieValue(anchor)`. Both this function's own docblock (lines 93-99) and `yorkie-json.ts:13-20` state that `detachYorkieValue` walks a Yorkie array proxy as an object and yields `{createdAt, movedAt}` CRDT metadata — exactly the wrong data for `pdf-text.rects` and `docs-range.posRange`, the two anchor shapes this fix targets. So on the failure path the API answers 200 with a silently wrong anchor rather than failing loudly, which `unwrapJson`'s docblock explicitly argues against ('silently returning that would turn a loud 500 into a 200 carrying wrong data').

verdict.reason: The guard is genuinely local to one controller and the cited sibling write paths reach the protected operation unguarded. `assertPlainTabId`/`UNSAFE_TAB_IDS` is defined and used only in worksheet-images.controller.ts (:51-55, :82, :95). Every cited sibling performs the same lookup-then-write with only a truthiness check: worksheet-charts.controller.ts:45-52 -> :106-110 (`ws.charts = {}`), worksheet-styles.controller.ts:50-57 -> :94, worksheet-dimensions.controller.ts:53-60 -> :136/181/226/271, worksheet-filter-pivot.controller.ts:43 -> :90/136, cells.controller.ts:88-89/:125-126, and comments.controller.ts:323-326 -> :330-332 inside doc.update. I searched for an alternative protection and found none that covers these paths: main.ts installs only a global ValidationPipe (no effect on raw string @Param), workspace-scope.guard.ts never references tabId, and a repo-wide grep for prototype-key handling surfaces no shared tab-id sanitizer. The only related mechanism is worksheet-structure.controller.ts:104-113, which uses key-membership via safeWorksheetRecordKeys — a different, stronger check in an uncited controller that guards none of the cited sites; it only makes the finding's "one of ~8" count imprecise, not wrong in substance. That controller's own docblock (:84-90) further corroborates prod reachability: through the Yorkie proxy get trap, keys like `toString` answer with a truthy function, so a truthiness-only guard admits them and the subsequent assignment lands on a non-worksheet object while the route answers 200. That is a real, normally-reachable wrong-behavior/data-not-persisted path around the new guard, i.e. major under the correctness rubric.

finding.summary: duplicateTab copies a worksheet verbatim, so charts/pivots on the copy still source the ORIGINAL tab id
finding.evidence: `const copy: Worksheet = { ...worksheet, comments: {} }; root.sheets[newTabId] = copy;` — only `comments` is cleared. A `SheetChart` carries `sourceTabId` (packages/sheets/src/model/workbook/worksheet-document.ts:20) and the editor creates self-sourced charts with `sourceTabId: tabId` (frontend sheet-view.tsx:421). After `POST /tabs/:tabId/duplicate`, every chart (and any `pivotTable`) on the copy still points at the source tab, so the duplicated tab renders the original tab's data and stops tracking edits made to the copy. The copy is therefore not an independent duplicate, which is what the endpoint advertises ("Copy a tab and its grid next to it").

verdict.reason: The finding's core factual claim — that duplicateTab stores the worksheet verbatim with only `comments` cleared, leaving charts/pivots pointing at the original tab — is not true of this repository. tab-ops.ts:183 creates `copy` with `comments: {}`, but lines 184-192 then rebuild `copy.charts`, repointing every chart whose `sourceTabId === tabId` to `newTabId` (line 189) while intentionally leaving foreign-sourced charts alone, and line 193 does `delete copy.pivotTable;` before `root.sheets[newTabId] = copy` at line 194. The pivot `kind` is likewise stripped from the new TabMeta (lines 177-178). The doc comment at lines 149-163 spells out this exact reasoning. Tests pin the behavior: tab-ops.spec.ts:228-231 asserts the self-sourced chart on the copy has `sourceTabId === copy.id` while the foreign one is unchanged and the source tab is untouched; tab-ops.spec.ts:242-249 asserts the copy's `pivotTable` and `kind` are undefined and that the copy is not a second pivot dependent. The only call site reaching this code is tabs.controller.ts:265 (POST /tabs/:tabId/duplicate), which invokes this same function, so no un-fixed alternate path exists.

finding.summary: `withSref` hands a live Yorkie array proxy to `cellAnchorToSref`, unlike every existing caller which detaches with `Array.from` first
finding.evidence: `withSref` passes `worksheet.rowOrder ?? []` and `worksheet.colOrder ?? []` straight into `cellAnchorToSref`, which calls `order.rowOrder.indexOf(anchor.rowId)` (packages/sheets/src/comment/anchor.ts:26-27). Both existing call sites detach first — `rowOrder: Array.from(ws.rowOrder ?? []) as string[]` at packages/frontend/src/app/documents/document-detail.tsx:276 and :763. If the array proxy does not expose `indexOf`, every `GET .../comments` and every sheet thread creation 500s. Counter-evidence I found: `root.tabOrder.indexOf(tabId)` is used on a live root proxy at document-detail.tsx:474, which suggests `indexOf` does exist and this is only a divergence from the established detach-first convention (plus an O(N) CRDT walk per thread on a dense axis). Flagging at low confidence for the verifier to settle.

verdict.reason: The described code is not present. `withSref` at packages/backend/src/api/v1/comments.controller.ts:711-722 already detaches both axis orders before calling `cellAnchorToSref`: `rowOrder: Array.from(worksheet.rowOrder ?? []) as string[]` (:717) and `colOrder: Array.from(worksheet.colOrder ?? []) as string[]` (:718) — precisely the `Array.from` convention the finding says is missing. The doc comment at :703-709 states the detach and its rationale. `withSref` is the only path from this controller into `cellAnchorToSref` (import at :46, sole call at :714; callers at :240 and :334 both route through it), so no undetached proxy reaches `order.rowOrder.indexOf(...)` at packages/sheets/src/comment/anchor.ts:26-27. A regression test at packages/backend/src/api/v1/comments.controller.spec.ts:169-195 injects a fake Yorkie array proxy (iterable, numeric length, indexed keys, no `indexOf`) and asserts the ref still resolves to 'B2', which would fail under the claimed defect. The O(N) CRDT-walk concern also does not hold: the proxy is read once per thread via its iterator and `indexOf` then runs on a plain array.
